clue.text: Big cask supplied in case of in-flight emergency

indicators.note: read as 'made supple', bent into a new shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A large barrel is handed out for passengers when a flight runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied' signals the anagram of BIG CASK. The definition is descriptive: the thing kept handy for airsick passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline seat pockets hold a paper bag for passengers who are airsick during a flight.

clue.text: Looked outside, very very hungry

indicators.note: one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to look fixedly is to stare

explanation.surface: Someone gazed out of doors, absolutely famished.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'very' is not emphasis: the first gives V, the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Starved, informally, means extremely hungry, ravenous.

clue.text: Raging inferno is cause of collateral damage

parts.note: a raging person is very angry, cross
an inferno is a blazing fire

explanation.surface: A blazing fire leads to unintended harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bystanders caught between opposing gunfire suffer the unintended harm of war.

clue.text: Drum for singing philanthropist carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

parts.note: Bono, singer with U2, is known for charity campaigns
g is the abbreviation for gram, a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A drum for a charitable singer, carrying a light load.
explanation.definitionFit: Bongos are small hand drums played in pairs.

clue.text: Grove mistakenly taking German composer for Russian politician

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside
something done mistakenly is jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: J S Bach was a German composer

explanation.surface: A man named Grove wrongly mistakes a German composer for a Soviet leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' makes GOREV from GROVE; 'taking' puts BACH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Gorbachev was the last leader of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Sci-fi classic's 'not much good without horse to back

indicators.note: to back is read as to go backwards, so the assembled letters are read from the end
used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: something not much good is poor
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A remark that a science-fiction film is poor when it lacks a horse to bet on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: COB goes inside POOR to give POCOBOR, and 'to back' reverses the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1987 film about a cyborg police officer is regarded as a science-fiction classic.

clue.text: Unstable, like the Cornish coast

definitions.meaning: Cornwall, in south-west England, has a craggy shoreline

explanation.surface: A shaky description of the seaside in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means wobbly or shaky, and also full of crags, as the cliffs of Cornwall are.

clue.text: Startling news-type of weevil, receiving honour, keeps quiet

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it inside

parts.note: the boll weevil is a cotton pest

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Surprising news: an insect gets a medal but says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SH sits inside MBE (MBSHE), which sits inside BOLL. The MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a sudden surprising piece of news.

clue.text: Get over being obvious

definitions.meaning: to pass over, as a hurdle

explanation.surface: Getting past something being plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a fence is to jump it; a clear point is plain and evident.

clue.text: Template for glib bird

parts.note: a pat answer is glib, too ready
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A model for a smooth-talking bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or guide to copy from, as a dressmaker uses.

clue.text: Humble origin of a foot ailment

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch of hardened skin on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone's lowly beginnings trace back to a sore foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the proverb that great oaks from little seeds grow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak tree grows from this small nut, the classic image of a modest start.

clue.text: Laid-back drunken bum comes in late

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it sits inside it

parts.note: late in the sense of not long ago, recent

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relaxed drunk vagrant turns up after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' makes UMB from BUM, and 'comes in' puts it inside RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means lying down or reclining, literally leaning back.

clue.text: Is no one turning in change for seer?

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word for change

parts.note: to change is to vary

indicators.note: turning means the letters for no and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether nobody will convert to a new outlook about a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses NO + I to ION; IS + ION goes inside VARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer foresees the future, as a prophetic dreamer with second sight does.

clue.text: Popular officer's wise to incarcerate regimental leader

indicators.note: locking someone up places them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a wise person is sage

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A well-liked officer is shrewd enough to jail the head of the regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes R from 'regimental'; 'to incarcerate' puts it inside SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarge is the familiar, colloquial name soldiers use for a sergeant.

clue.text: Tendency to wander

definitions.meaning: the general direction or gist of something
to move about aimlessly, carried along

explanation.surface: A habit of roaming about.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general tendency; to drift is to move aimlessly.

clue.text: Happen to substitute

definitions.meaning: to stand in for someone, filling their position

explanation.surface: An event that comes about as a replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: To take place is to occur; to take someone's place is to stand in for them.

clue.text: Set to introduce writer to English town

indicators.note: introducing one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: to set is to harden, as concrete does
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A group is about to present an author to a town in England.
explanation.walkthrough: HARPENDEN is a commuter town in Hertfordshire, north of London. 'Set' looks like a noun (a group) but is the verb harden.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpenden is a market town in Hertfordshire, in England.

clue.text: Once again beginning to be more sensible about money

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: saner means more sensible
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: Starting over by being more prudent with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but reverses SANER to RENAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or reviving, coming back into being.

clue.text: Mischief -lose it around 6.50

indicators.note: one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to dement is, in old use, to go mad, lose your mind
VI is the Roman numeral for six and L for fifty

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out when someone loses their temper at ten to seven.
explanation.walkthrough: '6.50' looks like a time but is Roman numerals VI and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilment is reckless mischief, behaviour worthy of a devil.

clue.text: Wounded Knee-brave to come out quits

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference to the Wounded Knee massacre, with an injured warrior ending level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wounded' looks like part of the place name Wounded Knee but is the anagram signal for KNEEBRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish with neither profit nor loss is to end up even, quits.

clue.text: It's baked by mistake

definitions.meaning: a type of large crusty bread loaf in Britain

explanation.surface: Something was cooked in an oven by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British loaf with a rounded top and slashes; it is also an embarrassing blunder.

clue.text: State capital of Louisiana's first with washbasin

indicators.note: says the initial letter comes at the front of the answer
the capital of a word is its initial letter

parts.note: to state is to aver, declare

explanation.surface: A remark about the capital city of Louisiana and a basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State capital of Louisiana' pretends to be Baton Rouge; actually 'State' is AVER and 'capital of Louisiana' is L, put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A laver is an old word for a large basin for washing, as in the Biblical temple.

clue.text: Bishop picking up a sledge for habitue

indicators.note: picking up something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a luge is a racing sledge

explanation.surface: A churchman collects a toboggan for a frequent visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses A + LUGE to EGULA, and 'picking' places it inside RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is someone who frequents a place, a regular customer.

clue.text: Deck with gold axe

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to axe is to cut off, lop

explanation.surface: Decorate something with a golden axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a verb (adorn) but is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: He wrote of lake and sea creature

parts.note: an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A writer describing a lake and a marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Tibia's location in sartorial statistic

definitions.meaning: the tibia is in the leg, on its inner side

explanation.surface: Where the shinbone is, in tailoring measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone lies within the lower leg's inner side; a tailor measures trouser length on the leg from crotch to ankle.

clue.text: Numbskull turned to dictator

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: turned means the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A fool converted to tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'to' is part of the wordplay, reversed to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbskull is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Lawyer comes to tea at country house

parts.note: DA, district attorney, is an American prosecuting lawyer
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A solicitor drops by for tea at a rural mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage or villa.

clue.text: Overstuff a location with sulphide

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for stuff is read backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Cramming too much into one place along with a chemical compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overstuff' reads as one word but splits: 'Over' reverses CRAM to MARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcasite is an iron mineral, a pale crystalline form of iron disulphide used in jewellery.

clue.text: About to dance with fish basket

parts.note: c (circa) means about
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Getting ready to dance while holding a basket of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket anglers carry their catch in.

clue.text: Acting head of state swallows a potentially dangerous mixer

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch who is absent or a minor

explanation.surface: A stand-in ruler downs a risky cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixer' suggests a drink at a party; it is a chemical used in reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added in a chemical reaction, some of which are hazardous.

clue.text: Vehicle turning right before performer

indicators.note: says the first piece comes ahead of the second
turning means the abbreviation for right is read backwards

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A car swinging right in front of an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a heavy farm vehicle used for pulling machinery.
